title: DTO decorators that validate nothing
summary: A class-validator DTO lets everything through because no ValidationPipe runs it. whitelist only strips unknown fields quietly, and transform turns path params into the declared type.

turns.user: CreateUserDto has @IsEmail but POST with email: "nope" still returns 201. why

assistant.body: TL;DR: decorators alone validate nothing. class-validator decorators only attach metadata to the class, and reading it and running the checks is the job of ValidationPipe. Register it globally in main.ts and every @Body() is checked against its DTO class. ValidationPipe also needs class-transformer, so install both. I added whitelist: true as well, which guarantees that a field the DTO does not declare, such as isAdmin, is rejected with a 400.

turns.user: email is rejected now. but isAdmin: true still gets 201. its gone from the response but you said 400?? silently dropping it is creepy, make it an error

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. whitelist: true strips properties that have no decorator and says nothing. To get a 400, add forbidNonWhitelisted: true, which only works together with whitelist. Note: a property with no decorator at all counts as unknown too, so give a field that needs no checks an @Allow().
sed -i '' 's/whitelist: true }/whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true }/' src/main.ts

turns.user: also GET /users/:id, i wrote id: number but find(u => u.id === id) never finds anything

assistant.body: id: number is a TypeScript annotation and converts nothing at run time. A path param is always a string, so "1" === 1 is false. Add transform: true to ValidationPipe and it converts the param to the declared number, and @Body() becomes a real CreateUserDto instance instead of a plain object. ParseIntPipe on each param works too, but one line in main.ts covers every route.
sed -i '' 's/forbidNonWhitelisted: true }/forbidNonWhitelisted: true, transform: true }/' src/main.ts
